source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Regular cleansing, infection assessment, and dressing changes, rather than leaving the site alone entirely as the family member is currently suggesting","B":"Allowing secretions to accumulate around the stoma freely, similar to what the family member's suggestion to leave the area alone would actually result in","C":"Avoiding any cleaning of the stoma site to prevent irritation, similar to what the family member is currently suggesting for this tracheostomy care","D":"Applying occlusive tape directly over the stoma opening, which is not the appropriate approach to this particular aspect of tracheostomy care"}}
source_row.rationale: Routine tracheostomy stoma care generally includes regular cleansing of the site (per facility protocol, often with sterile saline or a prescribed solution) to remove secretions and reduce infection risk, careful assessment for signs of infection, skin breakdown, or granulation tissue, and changing the tracheostomy dressing/ties as needed to keep the area clean and dry, supporting stoma healing and reducing complication risk.
